HOW THE TOOL CALLS WERE VERIFIED (this is the important part)
  Not by eye. A checker script extracted every "-> <tool> {json}" / "<- {json}" block from
  SKILL.md, references/tree-ir.md and references/design-spec.md, de-elided them structurally
  (block comments and "..." placeholders removed from arrays/objects, but NOT from inside real
  string values such as "markup": "<!-- wp:group ... -->"), then:
    * looked each tool name up in the REAL tool table imported from
      x-agent/mcp/dist/mcp/src/registry.js (the compiled registry.ts, so the same zod objects the
      MCP server serves), and
    * ran def.inputSchema.safeParse(args) on every request, and
    * asserted every top-level key of every shown response exists in def.outputSchema's shape.
  Final run: "checked 22 tool calls, 0 problem(s)" across the three files. The checker caught and
  I fixed real errors during authoring (e.g. wp_tokens_apply arguments are the flattened
  DesignTokens fields, not a nested object).

decisions.what: Every tool-call transcript in SKILL.md and the two references is machine-verified against the real zod schemas, not eyeballed. A checker imports TOOLS from x-agent/mcp/dist/mcp/src/registry.js, extracts each '-> tool {json}' block from the markdown, structurally removes elision placeholders (block comments, and '...' strings that are whole array/object members - never '...' inside a real string value), runs inputSchema.safeParse on the arguments, and asserts every top-level key of each shown response exists in that tool's outputSchema shape. Final state: 22 tool calls checked, 0 problems.
decisions.why: A skill whose transcripts do not validate teaches the model to make invalid calls. This makes 'the examples are correct' a checkable claim instead of an assertion, and it caught real mistakes while writing (wp_tokens_apply takes the flattened DesignTokens fields; wp_validate/wp_compile take {version, epoch, blocks} flattened rather than a nested tree).

decisions.what: All example material is measured off live Playground instances rather than recalled: manifest attribute schemas, theme tokens, pattern names and shapes, diagnostic message text, and compiled markup (driven through GET /harness with Playwright). Read-only calls only, against instances already booted by other tracks on :9410 and :9430; nothing was mutated, nothing was stopped.
decisions.why: The whole premise of the plugin is 'the instance is ground truth, never training-data memory'. Documentation that violates that premise teaches the opposite of what it says. It also caught two things memory would have got wrong: core/heading no longer declares a textAlign attribute (alignment is style.typography.textAlign, and the instance answers W_ATTR_UNKNOWN), and the theme ships four testimonial patterns, which changes the R7 example from 'nothing exists' to the far more useful 'rungs 1 and 2 deliver everything except the rating'.

decisions.what: bin/plugin-check.sh runs Plugin Check through @wp-playground/cli's `php` subcommand rather than its `wp-cli` Blueprint step. The step exists and works, but @wp-playground/cli 3.1.50 does not print what it captured, so `run-blueprint` with a wp-cli step produces an empty report. The script instead mounts a tiny run-cli.php that sets $GLOBALS['argv'] and requires /tmp/wp-cli.phar (put there by the Blueprint's extraLibraries:['wp-cli']), and runs it via `wp-playground-cli php -- /wordpress/x-plugin-check/run-cli.php`, which does stream stdout and stderr.
decisions.why: M7 asks for an observed `wp plugin check x-companion` result. WP-CLI is not installed on this machine and Docker is not running, so Playground is the only real path; and a check whose output you cannot read is not a check. Verified end to end: `wp plugin list` and `wp plugin check` both produce their real output through this route.

decisions.what: plugin-check.sh scans the DISTRIBUTION surface by default, passing --exclude-directories=tests,bin,fixtures to `wp plugin check`; --include-dev scans everything. Both numbers are recorded in deviations[].
decisions.why: Those three directories are development scaffolding that never ships to wordpress.org, and Plugin Check flags any .sh file at all as `application_detected` ('Application files are not permitted') - it flags this very script, and tests/run-all.sh, and fixtures/packages/build.sh. Scanning them makes the report describe a plugin nobody would ever submit. The exclusion is stated in the script header, printed to stderr on every run, and documented in x-companion/README.md, so the number is never presented without its scope.

decisions.what: x-companion/readme.txt is written to the wordpress.org readme standard (header block, Description, Installation, FAQ, Changelog) with `Tested up to: 7.1`.
decisions.why: Plugin Check reports `no_plugin_readme` as an ERROR without the file, and then `outdated_tested_upto_header` when the value trails the WordPress version the checker sees. The sandbox boots `--wp latest`, which currently resolves to 7.1; 6.9 produced 'Tested up to: 6.9 < 7.1'. This value must be bumped whenever the target WordPress moves - it is a release chore, not a constant.

decisions.what: SKILL.md's R7 worked example scaffolds `agent/testimonial-card`, not `agent/testimonial`.
decisions.why: `agent/testimonial` is already used by the factory track's live fixture (fixtures/trees/valid-with-agent-block.json and the M5 live test), with a different attribute set. Two documents describing the same block name with different attributes is worse than two clearly different blocks. tree-ir.md 7 documents `agent/testimonial` as measured from a live instance while that fixture was installed; SKILL.md 5 scaffolds a distinct block whose justification is the star rating.

The 6 WARNINGS (not errors, no action strictly required):

    Deliberate; it IS core's constant. 243 - DynamicHooknameFound: self::GUARDED_ACTION,

This track completed the skill and documentation half: SKILL.md per skill_contract (all ten rules verbatim, three worked examples with schema-verified transcripts), both references, both READMEs, readme.txt and a working Plugin Check runner. The e2e half - tests/e2e/from-prompt.sh, tests/e2e/from-design.sh, and the manual in-Claude-Code check that the skill triggers on 'build me a landing page on my WordPress site' - is owned by another track and was not attempted here.
deviations.why: Claiming `done` for a milestone whose acceptance list is half unexecuted would be false. Packaging (the third acceptance item) is verified and documented in x-agent/README.md.

deviations.spec_ref: tools/merge-progress.py TARGETS - the x-companion ledger only reads x-companion/.progress-fragments and tools/.progress-fragments
deviations.what: The companion-side deliverables of this work (x-companion/README.md with the five named M7 sections, readme.txt, bin/plugin-check.sh and the observed Plugin Check result) cannot be recorded in x-companion/PROGRESS.json from here: this track owns only x-agent/.progress-fragments/docs.json, and milestone ids from an x-agent fragment are filtered out of the companion ledger by design. M7_hardening_and_docs in x-companion/PROGRESS.json therefore still needs a status from whoever owns x-companion/.progress-fragments/.
deviations.why: The fragment mechanism deliberately scopes milestone ids per ledger so parallel tracks cannot pollute each other's. Recording the gap here is the honest alternative to writing into a file this track does not own.

deviations.what:
MEASURED, and worth the harness track knowing: window.__compile() SILENTLY DROPS blocks that are absent from the client-side registry and still returns all_valid:true. Observed on core-only-toolchain while the factory fixture agent/testimonial was installed - a tree with two agent/testimonial nodes inside two core/columns compiled to two EMPTY
elements, all_valid:true, invalid:[]. __registry() held 113 names against a manifest of 117. So the registry_gaps diff in wp_compile is not a nicety: without it a green compile ships an empty page. Both worked examples in tree-ir.md now document this with the real output.
deviations.why: Recorded as evidence for the session/harness track rather than as a defect to fix here: wp_compile's documented harness_gap refusal is exactly the right guard, and it is implemented. The note is here so nobody later 'simplifies' the diff away.

deviations.what: MEASURED, and it moved mid-authoring: on core-plus-suite, window.__registry() returned 113 names against a manifest of 175 (zero kadence/* registered) before the harness admin-context change landed, and 176 after it. Documentation written against the earlier measurement was rewritten. The current, verified statement in tree-ir.md 4 and 6 and in x-companion/README.md is: Kadence registers only because the harness route defines WP_ADMIN for that request, which is ON in toolchain posture and OFF in production, so an identical suite tree can compile on a sandbox and return harness_gap against production. Also measured: four blocks are in __registry() but NOT in the manifest (kadence/countdown-inner, kadence/countdown-timer, kadence/pane, kadence/tab) - JS-only inner blocks, which validate as E_UNKNOWN_BLOCK.
deviations.why: Documenting a snapshot of a system three other agents are still changing means re-measuring before finalising. Both numbers are recorded so the change is traceable rather than looking like an authoring error.

deviations.what: FIXTURE DEFECT for the fixture-owning track: invalid-attr-enum.json sets textAlign:'justify' on core/heading to provoke E_ATTR_ENUM, but current WordPress core no longer declares a textAlign attribute on core/heading (alignment moved to style.typography.textAlign). Against a live instance the fixture produces W_ATTR_UNKNOWN and valid:true - it does not exercise E_ATTR_ENUM at all. A working substitute, verified live: core/button with tagName:'div' inside core/buttons, which returns E_ATTR_ENUM at /blocks/0/innerBlocks/0/attributes/tagName, 'must be one of a, button.' Not fixed here - x-agent/fixtures/ is not this track's file.
deviations.why: The spec requires one invalid fixture per Diagnostics error code; this one silently does not cover its code, so a regression in enum checking would pass the suite.

deviations.spec_ref: agent-plugin.spec.json skill_contract.worked_examples_required[1] ('from-design ... with one deliberate token-snap delta')
deviations.what: The from-design example's wp_spec_validate and wp_tokens_apply calls are real and schema-verified, and the spec body is fixtures/specs/hero-sample.json (which really does validate clean). The wp_verify RESPONSE in that example - box_tree, a11y_outline and the three diffs - is constructed rather than captured, and is marked as abbreviated in the text. wp_verify's handler module (src/tools/verify.ts) landed from the oracle track while this was being written and no live oracle run against a rendered hero was performed here.
deviations.why: Honesty about which bytes are measured and which are illustrative. The numbers shown are internally consistent (54px observed vs 3.5rem/56px snapped = +2px, outside the 1px font tolerance) and every field name is checked against wp_verify's real outputSchema, but they were not read off a browser.
